---
title: "Physics by Construction"
---

Physics by Construction teaches physics by building it. Every concept comes
with code you can run. The path leads from numerical simulation, through
experiments driven by AI agents, to formal proofs in Lean. Every listing,
figure, and proof on this site is produced or checked by the same pipeline
that publishes it.

The site is written for readers who already know undergraduate mechanics and
can program. It does not teach either again. It teaches what happens when you
combine them: modelling, numerical methods, experiments run by agents, and
formal verification, all applied to physics.

## Three pillars

1. **Simulate.** State a model and its assumptions, write it as a short
   Python program, and compare the result with what theory predicts.
2. **Experiment with agents.** Let an AI agent propose hypotheses and run
   the same simulation code to test them, on your own machine with your own
   API key.
3. **Prove.** State the result as a theorem in Lean 4 with Mathlib and check
   the proof by machine.

## One result, three ways

Take a mass $m$ on a spring with stiffness $k$. Its total energy is

$$
E = \frac{1}{2} m v^{2} + \frac{1}{2} k x^{2}.
$$

A simulation shows whether a numerical method keeps $E$ constant, and how
quickly it drifts when it does not. An agent can search for the time step at
which the drift becomes visible. A proof settles what the model itself
guarantees, for every initial condition at once.

## Lessons

The [learning path](path/index.qmd) lists every lesson in order, with its
difficulty and what it builds on. The first course, mechanics with numerical
simulation, is being written; lessons appear on the path as they pass
verification.
